title: India's Commonwealth Games Hockey Coach Gurdial Singh Bhangu Passes Away at 86
indian_angle: The passing of Gurdial Singh Bhangu, a coach instrumental in India's historic Commonwealth Games women's hockey victory, is a significant loss for Indian sports.
summary: Gurdial Singh Bhangu, the revered coach behind India's memorable 2002 Commonwealth Games women's hockey gold, has died at the age of 86.

title: Velavan Senthilkumar Exits London Open Squash in Quarterfinals
indian_angle: Indian player Velavan Senthilkumar's performance in the London Open is closely followed by Indian squash fans.
summary: World No 42 Velavan Senthilkumar, the second seed, was defeated 11-13, 6-11, 7-11 in the men's quarterfinals of the London Open squash tournament.

title: Hardik Pandya Out of Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Due to Shin Injury
indian_angle: This injury setback for Hardik Pandya is a concern for Indian cricket fans, especially with the T20 World Cup approaching.
summary: Star all-rounder Hardik Pandya has withdrawn from the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy after suffering a fresh shin injury, further delaying his return ahead of the T20 World Cup.

title: Jaiswal Hits Second Century on A Tour, Regains Form for Test Series
indian_angle: Yashasvi Jaiswal's return to form is a positive sign for the Indian Test team ahead of their upcoming series.
summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal scored his second century of the A tour (102 off 138 balls), signaling his return to sublime touch before the Test series begins on November 19.

title: BCCI Pays Tribute to Mohammed Shami, Hailing His Era-Defining Pace Bowling
indian_angle: The BCCI's tribute acknowledges Mohammed Shami's significant contribution to Indian Test cricket's pace attack.
summary: The BCCI honored Mohammed Shami, stating his career defined an era of Indian pace bowling and highlighting his impact on Test cricket.

title: East Bengal Becomes First Indian Club to Reach AFC Women's Champions League Knockouts
indian_angle: This is a historic achievement for an Indian club, marking a significant milestone for women's football in the country.
summary: East Bengal has made history by becoming the first Indian club to advance to the knockout stage of the AFC Women's Champions League, despite a 0-2 loss to April 25 SC.
